title: KV-COBRA: KV Cache Compression via Co-Optimized Bit-Rank Allocation
claim: Compression budget needs are heterogeneous across components, so uniform allocation is suboptimal and per-component optimization with variance-equalizing rotation is justified.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, each a plot with caption label beneath
description: Three side-by-side plots motivating per-head bit-rank allocation. Panel (a) is a log-scale eigenvalue spectrum against SVD direction. One dark curve for the highlighted head sits over seven grey curves. A pink shaded 'keep' region lies left of a dashed red vertical line, and a grey 'truncate' region lies to its right. A red annotation marks r*=56, b*=5. Panel (b) is a dense red bar chart of per-head distortion across about 256 heads. It has a dotted median line and a 'max/min ≈123×' label, and one tall spike stands out near the right end. Panel (c) is a bar chart of per-channel variance. A tall beige bar at channel 0 (SVD basis) decays quickly, while red bars after Hadamard rotation stay flat near the mean. The palette is red, beige and grey.
caption: (a) Spectrum sets (r⋆, b⋆): one head (dark) against the layer’s 7 others (grey). (b) Heads differ dramatically: per-head D at uniform 2 bpd spans 100× across 256 KV heads. (c) Hadamard flattens variance: per-channel, retained subspace, before (beige) and after (red).
abstract: What limits KV-cache compression at extreme bit-rates? We argue that it is not the choice of compression scheme, but how its budget is allocated across attention heads. Existing methods apply rank and bit-width uniformly, ignoring that each head has a different optimal mix of rank truncation and quantization. We show that co-optimizing rank and bit-width per head, using only standard low-rank projection and scalar quantization, dominates uniform allocation, with the largest gains at low bit-rates. Our method, KV-COBRA (Co-Optimized Bit-Rank Allocation), formalizes this as a resource-allocation problem: it balances rank-truncation loss against quantization loss within each head, then redistributes budget across heads to minimize total distortion. A fused Hadamard rotation equalizes per-channel variance, and reordering the SVD basis by attention-KL importance makes the solver query-aware. The same allocator extends to joint $K{+}V$ compression. On perplexity, zero-shot, and long-context benchmarks from $0.5$ to $4$ bits per dimension (bpd), KV-COBRA shows the smallest accuracy degradation among evaluated methods at low bpd, with no per-token overhead.
